landing.hero_title: Which crop rotation suits your particular field?
landing.hero_text: Compare 3–4 crop rotations and see what each does for soil, water and income over 3–5 years. The calculation uses NASA satellite data for your field and agronomic rules with cited sources.
landing.cta_own: Try it on your own field
landing.cta_demo: Demo: a field in Akmola Region
landing.problem_lead: Northern Kazakhstan depends almost entirely on one crop, and this exhausts the land.
landing.problem_1: In the northern regions wheat takes up to 87 % of the sown area. A fall in world prices or a crop failure is a serious economic risk.
landing.problem_2: Soil is degrading. According to the drafters of the bill “On Soil Protection”, potential soil fertility has fallen by 17 %, and the loss of humus on arable land is becoming irreversible. Experts estimate that more than 75 % of soils in use are degraded, and the yield shortfall from exhausted arable land costs about $2.4 billion.
landing.problem_3: Raising humus content by even 1 % takes 50–100 years. The priority is to prevent losses now.
landing.problem_4: Drought strikes regularly. In 2021 it cut the grain harvest to about 15.3 million t versus 20 million t in 2020. In 2023 a regional emergency was discussed.
landing.state_title: The state is already moving in the right direction
landing.state_text: In two years the wheat area was cut by almost 730 thousand ha. Legumes enrich the soil with nitrogen and raise the yield of the following crops. Flax and rapeseed sell from 200 thousand tenge/t versus 65–70 thousand tenge/t for wheat. Food Contract Corporation launched forward financing for the shift to legumes in Akmola, Kostanay and North Kazakhstan regions.
landing.why_title: Why the problem is not solved
landing.why_1: General recommendations are issued for the whole region, while every field has its own moisture, rainfall and history.
landing.why_2: The transition is risky: the wrong year or field can cost a harvest.
landing.why_3: NASA satellite data are free but complex and in English.
landing.why_4: There is no tool that connects satellite data, scientific recommendations and the farmer's priorities.
landing.how_1: Draw the field on the map or upload its boundary.
landing.how_2: Enter what was sown in recent years and what matters more to you: income, moisture or soil.
landing.how_3: Compare the options: soil, water, income and risk scores, a year-by-year projection and a drought stress test.
landing.for_2: Akimats and agriculture departments — to see where diversification has the greatest effect.
landing.for_3: Food Contract Corporation, banks and insurers — to assess financing risks.
landing.change_1: Decisions based on the data of a specific field, not on “what the neighbour does”.
landing.change_2: The state diversification programme reaches every farm.
landing.change_3: Soil that is almost impossible to restore is protected.

compare.weighted_hint: Scores multiplied by the weights of priority “{{priority}}”: soil {{soil}}, water {{water}}, income {{income}}, risk {{risk}}.

scores.scale: Scale 1–5: from the worst ({{min}}) to the best ({{max}}) value among {{n}} options (compared options and default options).
scores.formula_soil: Soil index = 100 + Σ over years (nitrogen balance / 10 kg + humus balance / 0.25 t) − 2 points for every year of cereal monoculture from the third
scores.formula_water: Mean plan water deficit = crop seasonal need − (May–August precipitation + pre-sowing moisture stock). The stock is larger after fallow.
scores.formula_income: Income = Σ (yield × price − costs). Yield = base × region index × (1 + predecessor effect) × (1 + monoculture penalty) × moisture coefficient (FAO-33: 1 − Ky·(1 − W/need)).
scores.formula_risk: Risk = mean share of revenue lost if one plan year turns out dry. The higher the crop's Ky, the larger the loss.

forecast.note: Prices and costs are held constant over the plan. Weather is the field's normal year (25-year median).

stress.intro: Choose which plan year turns out dry, like {{year}}. Each crop's yield falls according to its Ky coefficient (FAO).
stress.chart: Income over the plan, thousand KZT/ha

warnings.smap_threshold_fallback: No SoilGrids data: the SMAP dryness threshold {{value}} m³/m³ comes from the rules, not from the field's wilting point.

methodology.title: Methodology and sources
methodology.lead: The model is simple and transparent: only the rules in the tables below, no machine learning. Every number has a source and a status.
methodology.counts: Total values: {{total}}. Verified: {{verified}}. Assumptions needing review: {{assumption}}.
methodology.model_1: Yield = crop base yield × region index × (1 + predecessor effect) × (1 + monoculture penalty) × field moisture coefficient.
methodology.model_2: Moisture coefficient per FAO-33: relative yield = 1 − Ky × (1 − W / need). W = May–August precipitation + pre-sowing moisture stock. Coefficient = yield at field moisture / yield at the region's normal moisture.
methodology.model_3: Pre-sowing moisture stock = region norm × (SMAP April–May moisture / its median), but not more than the soil water-holding capacity from SoilGrids (Saxton & Rawls, 2006). Without SMAP, NASA POWER September–April precipitation is used instead.
methodology.model_4: Income = yield × price − costs. Soil index = 100 + nitrogen balance / 10 kg + humus balance / 0.25 t for every year.
methodology.model_5: Scores 1–5 are normalised from the worst to the best value among compared and default options. The farmer's priority sets the score weights.
methodology.model_6: Dry year: May–August precipitation below the 20th percentile of the 1991–2020 normal or a standardised anomaly ≤ −1.
methodology.limit_1: Prices and costs are constant over the plan; inflation, subsidies and market swings are not considered.
methodology.limit_2: Fertilisers, varieties, sowing dates and crop protection are not considered: the model compares rotations under the same technology.
methodology.limit_3: Field moisture is estimated from data with 9–50 km cells: local showers and field relief are not visible.
methodology.limit_4: Most agronomic coefficients are assumptions. They are flagged and must be checked by an agronomist and against data of the A. I. Barayev Research Centre.
methodology.limit_5: Predecessor effects come from trials in Canada (an analogue region). Transferring them to Kazakhstan is an assumption.
methodology.todo_title: Sources that still need a link
methodology.evidence_counts: By evidence: confirmed by sources — {{literature}}, agronomist review needed — {{agronomist_review}}, preliminary assumptions — {{preliminary}}, definitions and calculations — {{definition}}.
methodology.audit_link: Model audit report: docs/MODEL_AUDIT.md in the repository.
methodology.limit_6: A 3–5-year horizon truncates the benefit of fallow and of a legume in the last plan year: their costs are counted, but the following crop's gain is not.
methodology.limit_7: Yields and costs of alternative crops are assumptions. If they turn out 20–30 % worse than assumed, wheat monoculture may be more profitable (see docs/MODEL_AUDIT.md).

nasa.title: NASA data in Agro-Sevooborot
nasa.subtitle: Which datasets are integrated, what they measure and where their limits are

pitch.problem: In Kazakhstan's northern regions wheat takes up to 87 % of the sown area, and droughts like 2021 recur. Farmers need a way to compare diversified rotations using their own field's data rather than regional averages.
pitch.approach: A transparent rule-based model: every number lives in YAML with a source and a verification status. NASA data set the moisture and drought frequency of the specific field; the rules set the crop response. No machine learning and no black box.
pitch.data: Connection status for each catalog entry is loaded from the running service — see the list below for limits and why a source is not connected yet.

nasa.datasets_hint: Status comes from the service: connected (in use), planned (not wired yet), key required (Earthdata or similar), or offline (demo / no network). Icons and labels repeat the state, not only colour.
nasa.states_legend: Status labels (each card above shows the live state from the server):
nasa.offline_note: The server is in offline mode; live NASA requests are not made until it is turned off.
nasa.honest_1: NASA POWER precipitation and temperature are a reanalysis in a ~50 km cell: the district's climate, not a weather station on the field.
nasa.honest_2: SMAP measures the top 5 cm of soil in a 9 km cell; the moisture stock of the 1 m layer is estimated by the model.
nasa.honest_3: MODIS NDVI shows green biomass and is used for monitoring only; it does not measure yield.
nasa.honest_4: All series are historical, with data-delivery latency; the service makes no weather forecasts.
nasa.honest_earthdata: Some NASA datasets require a NASA Earthdata account and an approved application before data can be read — the cards above show which sources need it.
